proposals.before: In Kangxi 8 the Kangxi emperor, on Verbiest's advice, commissioned six new instruments: ecliptic theodolite, equatorial theodolite, azimuth theodolite, altitude quadrant, astronomical quadrant, and celestial globe.
proposals.after: In Kangxi 8 the Kangxi emperor, on Verbiest's advice, commissioned six new instruments: ecliptic theodolite, equatorial theodolite, azimuth theodolite, altitude quadrant, sextant, and celestial globe.
proposals.reason: 紀限儀 is a sixty-degree instrument (one sixth of a circle), i.e. a sextant, not a quadrant; s0063 confirms the arc is 六十度 / one sixth of a circle.

proposals.before: The half ring borne above, front and rear running true north-south, rises straight to the celestial pole and cuts the horizon at center.
proposals.after: The half ring borne above, front and rear running true north-south, rises straight to the zenith and cuts the horizon at center.
proposals.reason: 天頂 means zenith, not celestial pole (北極).

proposals.before: The line within the axle is always the plumb line to the celestial pole.
proposals.after: The line within the axle is always the plumb line to the zenith.
proposals.reason: 天頂 means zenith; the idiomatic already correctly says zenith plumb line.

proposals.before: The astronomical quadrant's arc is one sixth of a circle, graduated to sixty degrees.
proposals.after: The sextant's arc is one sixth of a circle, graduated to sixty degrees.
proposals.reason: An arc of one sixth of a circle (六十度) is a sextant; calling 紀限儀 a quadrant contradicts the stated geometry.

proposals.before: A single ring leans obliquely as the fixed ecliptic equator circle; both faces are engraved with the circuit of the sun's twelve hours; zi and wu noon rightly occupy the meridian double ring's hollow half, knotting at its midpoint—that is celestial latitude.
proposals.after: A single ring leans obliquely as the fixed celestial equator circle; both faces are engraved with the circuit of the sun's twelve hours; zi and wu noon rightly occupy the meridian double ring's hollow half, knotting at its midpoint—that is celestial latitude.
proposals.reason: 天常赤道圈 is the fixed celestial equator ring, not an ecliptic equator; the idiomatic correctly says fixed equator.

proposals.before: Again according to the capital's north polar altitude in degrees and minutes, count upward to complete one quadrant—that is the celestial pole.
proposals.after: Again according to the capital's north polar altitude in degrees and minutes, count upward to complete one quadrant—that is the zenith.
proposals.reason: 天頂 means zenith; counting a quadrant up from polar altitude yields the zenith, matching the idiomatic.

proposals.before: At the celestial pole set a small nail to suspend the plumb line; the plumb rightly reaches the earth's center and also rightly cuts the double ring's face.
proposals.after: At the zenith set a small nail to suspend the plumb line; the plumb rightly reaches the earth's center and also rightly cuts the double ring's face.
proposals.reason: 天頂 means zenith; a plumb is suspended from the zenith toward the nadir.

decisions.reason: s0005 lists 紀限儀 among the six remade instruments; s0063 states its arc is 全圓六分之一 / 六十度, i.e. a sextant. Rendering it as 'astronomical quadrant' contradicts that geometry; 'sextant' is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 紀限儀，弧面為全圓六分之一，分六十度

decisions.reason: s0011 has 上直天頂; 天頂 is the zenith, not the celestial pole (北極). The prior literal misreads it; 'rises straight to the zenith' matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.
s0050 says 恆為天頂之垂線; 天頂 means zenith. 'Plumb line to the celestial pole' is wrong; 'plumb line to the zenith' restores the sense already correct in the idiomatic.
s0063 itself defines 紀限儀 as an arc of one sixth of a full circle divided into sixty degrees. Calling it an 'astronomical quadrant' contradicts that definition; 'sextant' is the correct English term.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 弧面為全圓六分之一，分六十度

decisions.reason: s0086 names the ring 天常赤道圈, the fixed celestial equator, not an ecliptic equator. 'Fixed ecliptic equator circle' invents an ecliptic sense absent from the Chinese; 'fixed celestial equator circle' matches 天常赤道圈.
s0091 ends 即天頂 after counting one quadrant up from the capital's north polar altitude. 天頂 is the zenith, not the celestial pole; the proposed replacement matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上數至成一象限，即天頂

decisions.reason: s0093 places the nail 于天頂 to hang the plumb toward 地心. 天頂 is the zenith; suspending from the celestial pole would misstate both the Chinese and the geometry of a plumb.
